newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-BTP vols gallop on as futures see-saw.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-BTP vols gallop on as futures see-saw.

text.p: Implied volatility of Italian BTP options continued higher on Friday as the underlying futures market yo-yoed in a 100 basis point range, traders said.
"We've seen volatility just cracked up in the past few days," said an options trader at an Italian bank in London.
He said at-the-money straddles were trading at an implied volatility of around 8.0 percent by mid-morning trade.
"Out-of-the-money calls are trading at very high volatility," he added.
December BTP futures on LIFFE see-sawed in early trade, gaining 62 basis points at one stage to reach a 123.67 high.
By 1040 GMT the contract had slipped back and was quoted 14 basis points lower on the day at 122.91.

Analysts said comments from Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini earlier that he expected the lira to return soon to the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) had fuelled the early rally, but profit-takers soon came in to cash up.
Later, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said Italy would begin talks on lira re-entry to the ERM "as soon as possible".
Prodi also called for "immediate, rapid" talks over the level of the lira at re-entry.
By around 1115 GMT, Steven West, a BTP options broker at GNI in London said BTP option straddles were trading at an implied vol of 8.15 percent.
"That is pretty high considering that it was trading about 6.5 percent about two-and-a-half weeks ago," he said.
West said the main focus for the market this session would be September non-farm payrolls data due form the U.S. at 1230 GMT. "A lot hinges on those numbers," he said.

"If we get a particularly strong number then obviously the (futures) markets will give back a lot of their gains. But if it is soft -- as many people expect it to be -- then we could see the futures start to rally again, in which case volatility might continue its upward trend."
Analysts polled by Reuters are forecasting that 166,000 jobs will have been added to the payroll in September, versus a 250,000 gain in August.

The Italian bank's trader said implied vols were likely to stay high for the near term -- especially in the front-month conracts -- since the Italian market was proving very sensitive to talk about European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU)
"With the movements we have seen in the past few days (in the futures market) it is not surprising that volatility has gone so far," he said.
Implied vols on December BTP options started the week at around 7.3 percent.

"Every time somebody has made a comment about Italy and EMU the market has jumped around," he said. "And as long as that continues -- and it should do for quite a while -- volatility will keep a better bid."
